jobs_results.description:
About us


One Off Robotics builds some of the largest robotic metal 3D printing systems in the industry, and we run them as a service. Based in Chattanooga, Tennessee, our team of engineers, designers and builders designs, wires, programs and commissions large-format robotic additive manufacturing work cells, then puts them to work producing real metal parts for customers.


The role


You'll write the software that makes our robotic work cells run, from the PLC and robot controller up to the Windows applications our operators use every day. You'll work across the whole stack and help shape how our software is architected as we scale from a few systems to many.


What you'll do



 Program and maintain PLC logic for cell control, sequencing, I/O and safety interlocks
 Program industrial robots, with a focus on ABB robots
 Design, build and maintain Windows desktop applications in .NET (C#) that integrate with robots, PLCs and process equipment
 Help define and evolve our software architecture so it stays maintainable, testable and scalable
 Commission, debug and support systems on our shop floor and at customer sites
 Work closely with our electrical and mechanical engineers to bring new cells online
 Use AI tools every day to write, review, test and document code faster

What we're looking for



 4+ years of professional experience in industrial automation or robotics software (senior candidates: 8+ years, with experience owning a system's architecture)
 Hands-on PLC programming experience (Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff or similar)
 Industrial robot programming experience; ABB robots and Kuka robots preferred
 Strong C# / .NET skills building Windows applications
 A solid grasp of software architecture: clean structure, interfaces between systems, and designing for change
 Comfortable reading electrical schematics and working next to live equipment
 Self-starter who takes ownership, communicates clearly and works well on a small team
 Willing to travel to customer sites for installation and commissioning

Nice to have



 Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics or similar, or equivalent experience
 AI proficiency
 ABB RobotStudio, offline programming or simulation experience
 Industrial communication protocols (EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus, OPC UA)
 Experience with HMIs, data logging, machine vision or process monitoring

job_highlights.title: Responsibilities
items: You will join a team of talented and passionate engineers developing, testing, and optimizing the software and firmware running on our various robot platforms

As a Robotics Engineer on the Simulation team, you will build the pipelines and infrastructure that let us simulate UR cobots and MiR mobile robots at scale — before a single unit is deployed on a customer floor
Simulation is central to how we reduce integration time, validate fleet behaviour, and let customers model their own environments and workflows ahead of deployment

You will work with ROS2, physics engines, and GPU-accelerated simulation to turn real robotic systems into faithful virtual ones, and you will build the tooling, services, and pipelines that make those simulations reliable, repeatable, and fast

You will collaborate closely with research scientists working on world models and 3D scene generation, with application engineers who understand real customer deployments, and with the wider R&D organization in Denmark and Bangalore
Design, build, and maintain the simulation pipeline and supporting infrastructure used to model UR and MiR robot platforms in virtual environments
Develop and maintain accurate robot models — kinematics, dynamics, sensors, and controllers — ensuring simulated behaviour faithfully reflects real hardware
Implement and optimise ROS2-based integrations so simulated robots interoperate seamlessly with the same software stack that runs on physical systems
Build scalable simulation infrastructure across cloud and on-premises GPU environments, including job orchestration, environment versioning, and resource management
Develop tooling and services that allow engineers, application teams, and customers to configure, launch, monitor, and analyse simulation runs
Build capabilities for importing customer models and environments, and for creating custom scenarios and workflows
Contribute to multi-agent simulation supporting fleet-level coordination, zone layout, and multi-robot interaction scenarios
Establish automated testing, validation, and benchmarking frameworks that measure simulation fidelity and tie results to integration time and fleet performance
Work with research scientists to integrate world models and generated 3D scenes into production simulation workflows
Write clean, well-tested, and documented code, and participate actively in code reviews to uphold engineering standards across the team
Contribute to CI/CD pipelines and deployment tooling that keep simulation systems reliable and continuously validated
Partner with product, application, and customer-facing teams to translate real deployment challenges into simulation capabilities
Solid understanding of robotics fundamentals — kinematics, dynamics, control, coordinate transforms, and sensor modelling

jobs_results.description: Our Purpose TERADYNE, where experience meets innovation and driving excellence in every connection. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better business results.   Universal Robots, part of Teradyne Robotics, is the world market leader in collaborative robots (cobots), making products that empower our customers and positively transform the way they work. Teradyne Robotics is a division of Teradyne and includes Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots (MiR). Our global R&D organization of 200+ engineers builds the software and systems behind every cobot we ship. Mandatory Qualifications:   Bachelor's or Master's degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.   2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with meaningful time spent working on robotics systems.   Strong programming proficiency in Python and C++, with a demonstrated ability to write production-quality, maintainable code.   Hands-on experience with ROS or ROS2, including building nodes, working with the middleware, and integrating with robot hardware or simulators.   Practical experience with at least one robotics simulation environment (e.g. Gazebo, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Webots, or CoppeliaSim). Physics engines and their tuning for contact-rich or high-fidelity robotic interaction (PhysX, Bullet, ODE, MuJoCo).   Cloud infrastructure and orchestration — AWS, Azure, or GCP, with Docker and Kubernetes.   Mobile robotics concepts including SLAM, navigation stacks, path planning, and fleet management.   Manipulator robotics including motion planning, trajectory generation, and collision checking.   3D geometry, scene representation, and asset pipelines (USD, URDF, SDF, mesh processing).   Multi-agent or fleet-scale simulation and the coordination challenges it introduces.   Backend service development and distributed systems design.   Data pipelines and time-series or large-scale sensor data handling.   Machine learning workflows and experience deploying trained models into production systems.   Digital twin development and sim-to-real validation methodologies.   Real-time systems, embedded software, or robot firmware development. An early-stage team building autonomous, off-grid power plants for the AI era.

You are the engineer who prefers dirt and high voltage to simulation loops, eager to deploy robots that construct critical infrastructure without a grid connection. This role demands hands-on ownership of electrical and mechatronic systems that operate autonomously in rugged construction environments. You will write embedded firmware in C/C++ to bridge the gap between heavy industrial machinery and intelligent decision-making.
